title: Framework tour & judgment, cost/latency controls, STAR stories I
objective: AutoGen, Google ADK, AWS Strands tour; build the same toy agent in two frameworks and defend a choice by failure modes. Cost/latency controls in Paper-to-Prod. First six STAR stories. Code-assistant design case.
topics: Framework tour (Ed Donner Wk5); selection judgment
Caching across steps; per-step model routing; parallel tool calls; run budgets; kill-switches
STAR stories: ownership, conflict, failure, ambiguity, leadership, learning
SD-B2 case: design a code assistant (context strategy, latency budget)
theory: Ed Donner Week 5; Googleyness & Leadership rubric.
deliverables: Same toy agent in 2 frameworks + docs/framework-choice.md (failure modes, not popularity)
Paper-to-Prod: per-run cost cut ≥40% with before/after data
checkpoint: Defend a framework choice to a skeptic

knowledge: What does ADK abstract that Strands does not (or vice versa)?

tasks.text: Ed Donner Agentic Week 5: rapid-fire tour (AutoGen, Google ADK, AWS Strands). Skim each architecture page; note the abstraction each adds and what it hides.
STAR stories 1–3 (ownership, conflict, failure) from your real MERN + build history. Each: Situation → Task → Action → Result with a number; your decisions emphasized.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Balanced Binary Tree (Easy) — no notes, ≤35 min each, narrate, state complexity; log time vs first pass.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Ed Donner Agentic Week 5: rapid-fire tour (AutoGen, Google ADK, AWS Strands)” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.

Build the same toy agent (3 tools, one handoff) in two of {ADK, Strands, AutoGen}; docs/framework-choice.md: which for Paper-to-Prod and why, argued by failure modes (state loss, tool errors, observability, cost).
SD-B2 case: design a code assistant (repo context strategy, retrieval, latency budget, caching, eval) — 45-min run → delta.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Same Tree (Easy, B75) — no notes, ≤35 min each, narrate, state complexity; log time vs first pass.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Build the same toy agent (3 tools, one handoff) in two of {ADK, Strands, AutoGen}; docs/fr” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.

Paper-to-Prod: prompt caching across steps, cheaper model for planner/verifier where evals allow, parallel tool calls, run budgets + kill-switch; measure cost/run before/after on the 30-task suite at equal score. Target ≥40% cut.
STAR stories 4–6 (ambiguity, leadership/influence without authority, learning fast). Rehearse aloud; time each to 2 minutes.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Subtree of Another Tree (Easy, B75) — no notes, ≤35 min each, narrate, state complexity; log time vs first pass.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Paper-to-Prod: prompt caching across steps, cheaper model for planner/verifier where evals” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.
Write docs/when-not-to-agent.md for Paper-to-Prod: which parts became deterministic pipelines and why (reliability math from W36).
Second-pass DSA: 3 cold re-solves (mixed Trees/Graphs).
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.
Paper-to-Prod: scheduled weekly brief run (cron/queue), email/PDF delivery stub, feedback capture → eval data.
Pramp mock coding interview (weekly). Debrief.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST (Medium, B75) — no notes, ≤35 min each, narrate, state complexity; log time vs first pass.
Application pipeline (20 min): check saved searches, apply to 1–2 fitting roles within 48 h of posting, update tracker (status · next action · what failed).
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Paper-to-Prod: scheduled weekly brief run (cron/queue), email/PDF delivery stub, feedback ” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.
Record yourself telling stories 1–3; watch back; cut filler. Practice the disagreement script once this week at work (“I see it differently because X — happy to go with the team’s call”).
LinkedIn build-note: cost/run before vs after.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal (Medium, B75) — no notes, ≤35 min each, narrate, state complexity; log time vs first pass.

Weekly revision — Framework tour (Ed Donner Wk5); selection judgment, Caching across steps; per-step model routing; parallel tool calls; run budgets; kill-switches, STAR stories: ownership, conflict, failure, ambiguity, leadership, learning, SD-B2 case: design a code assistant (context strategy, latency budget): rewrite the key ideas from memory (no notes), then compare with your notes and fix the gaps. Reimplement two things from this week without looking.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Binary Tree Right Side View (Medium) · Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree (Medium) — ≤35 min each, narrate, log time.
Weekly review: answer this week’s knowledge questions aloud, run the practical checks, then write the three notes (struggled / learned / improve) in Weekly Plan → Review. Update the tracking sheet.

JS/MERN spaced recall (Cycle 3 · interview mode) · Event loop & async ordering: Interview mode: 2-min spoken answer ‘explain the event loop’, then implement Promise.all + Promise.race cold in ≤8 min. Log misses in mistakes.md; if you fail the check, redo the matching module in Side Tracks → 🟨 JavaScript & MERN Refresher.
Plan next week: read W41’s objective and Day 1; move any unfinished 🔴 task into next week’s Day 1; confirm calendar blocks. Then rest — consistency beats intensity.
